span.label: THE DOUBLE DISSOCIATION ITSELF, and it is two CURVES rather than two conditions: `within the SOA range from 42 to 98 ms: the amount of priming INCREASED, but recognition accuracy DETERIORATED with SOA`. No level of invisibility is asserted anywhere - the argument is carried entirely by the opposite slopes, which is the criterion Schmidt2011 later proposed as a replacement for requiring zero sensitivity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: `DIFFERENT TEMPORAL LAWS` - the general form of the claim, and it is a statement about SHAPES rather than about magnitudes: conscious perception and unconscious behavioural effects of the same masked stimuli do not merely differ in size, they are governed by different functions of time. Seventh record this sitting where a time course is the load-bearing variable, and the first where two time courses ARE the finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: SUBLIMINAL IN WHICH RESPECT - a precision most records in this corpus do not make: `prime stimuli were NOT subliminal in the sense that their presence or absence could not be detected, but the CRITICAL PRIME FEATURE remained perfectly invisible`. Something was plainly there to be seen; the attribute that did the priming was not. `Subliminal` is a predicate of a FEATURE here, not of a stimulus, and the difference decides what the effect is evidence for
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the priming time course is INDIFFERENT to whether the prime could be reported: `Quotation withheld` The masking function changes shape - type A to type B - and the priming function does not follow it. That is a stronger result than a difference in size at one delay, because it survives a change in the shape of the other curve

span.label: action priming —distinct-from→ visual awareness
span.note: differs in: THEIR TIME COURSES - measured under the same conditions, on the same stimuli, and found to obey different temporal laws. Over 42 to 98 ms priming rises while recognition falls, so neither can be a noisier reading of the other · strength of the relation: 0.95 — THE PAPER'S RESULT, and the empirical basis for the criterion Schmidt2011 proposes eight years later. Confidence 0.95 - the contrast is the study's design, stated in its own summary of what it did.
